Prepare a diet table for DietView (validate + add taxa)

Source: R/dv_prepare.R
dv_prepare.Rd

Validates the long table with dv_validate() and attaches the taxonomic lineage for the declared ranks. The taxonomy can come from:

  • "columns" - the rank columns are already in data;

  • "worms" - fetch the lineage from WoRMS by AphiaID/name;

  • "table" - join a lineage table you supply via lineage;

  • "auto" - use columns if present, else lineage if given, else WoRMS.

Ranks that cannot be resolved are kept as NA and later shown as an explicit unidentified category below the deepest identified rank – never dropped.

Usage

dv_prepare(
  data,
  spec,
  taxonomy = c("auto", "columns", "worms", "table"),
  lineage = NULL,
  fuzzy = TRUE,
  cache_dir = tools::R_user_dir("DietView", "cache"),
  cache_max_age = 180,
  strict_covariates = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame (the long diet table).

spec

A dietview_spec from dv_spec().

taxonomy

One of "auto", "columns", "worms", "table".

lineage

For taxonomy = "table": a data.frame with a key column (prey_id or prey_name, matching your spec) plus one column per rank.

fuzzy

For taxonomy = "worms": when the exact name fails, try WoRMS TAXAMATCH fuzzy matching (default TRUE). Fuzzy hits are flagged, never silent - review them with dv_taxonomy_report().

cache_dir

Cache directory for the WoRMS path. NULL disables caching.

cache_max_age

For the WoRMS path: cached lookups older than this many days are fetched again (default 180). See dv_taxonomy_worms().

strict_covariates

Passed to dv_validate(): if TRUE (default) a declared covariate missing from data is an error; if FALSE it is dropped from the returned spec with a warning.

verbose

Print progress and the validation summary.

Value

An object of class dietview_prep: a list with data, spec (minus any dropped covariates), ranks, taxonomy_source (the taxonomy path actually used) and taxonomy_log. When taxonomy = "worms", taxonomy_log is the per-prey provenance table, with the attributes retrieved (time of the run) and worrms_version; otherwise it is NULL.

Details

With taxonomy = "worms", each record is keyed by its AphiaID when it has one and by its own prey name otherwise, so records without an AphiaID never share a lineage by accident. Records with neither key stay fully unidentified, with a warning.

With taxonomy = "table", the lineage table must hold each key once (a duplicated key is an error), and prey keys absent from the table are reported with a warning before their records are treated as fully unidentified.

Examples

# the standard set-up: public ICES data, non-food items and nematodes dropped
phylum <- ices_lineage$phylum[match(ices_diet$prey_aphia_id, ices_lineage$prey_aphia_id)]
dat <- ices_diet[ices_diet$item_type != "non_food" & !phylum %in% "Nematoda", ]
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_common",
  predator_latin = "predator_latin",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "prey_aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "prey_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight_g",
  count          = "prey_count",
  digestion      = "digestion_label",
  covariates     = c("region", "year", "quarter")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                   verbose = FALSE)
prep
#> <dietview_prep>
#>   records   : 8530 
#>   stomachs  : 4222 
#>   predators : 22 
#>   ranks     : kingdom > phylum > class > order > family > genus > species 
#>   covariates: region, year, quarter 
#>   source    : table 
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# online: resolve prey against WoRMS (needs 'worrms' + internet)
prep_worms <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "worms")
} # }
